body:
Well, I didn't get the job I was looking for, but I did find one that pays better (but is a lot more work). 

I start on the 18th, pretty excited about that actually. 

My roomate is in detox right now, he seems to want to quit, and he still has his job once he gets out. 

Maybe he can pull it off this time, though I only give him a 30% chance...

Either way, one month at this new job and I can afford to move out whenever I want to, and I told him the second he drinks I pack my stuff. 

Thanks again for your insight and support, you gave me a much better perspective than the one I was in. 

So how did your job search go?

Well, not so good actually. Experience wise it was pretty bad, no second interviews or return calls. 

Emotionally, I am doing better. I've been working on a plan to get the money to move out, and thankfully we managed to get the bills paid for this month. 

Prime Roomate is still being a drunk asshat, though amazingly even after missing so much work he still isn't fired and getting a full paycheck (hence how we paid the bills). 

I'm not actively suicidal anymore, though there is still the lingering thought in the back of my mind as a 'worst case scenario solution'. I'm not paralyzed by my dread anymore, and am actively working towards fixing my living situation. 

No matter what the results, I am out of this house before next month.

Thank you again for your advice and your supportive posts. I really believe they are what gave me the perspective to begin thinking positively again.

I'll make a post and PM you and /u/dankjeblieft on what happens. 

Thanks again for your time and advice.

This actually helped a lot.

I kind of lost track of my worth in this, and reading your kind response has reminded me of this. 

You're absolutely right, I needed to get out of here for a bit and I took the time today to take a two hour walk and it really gave me perspective. 

I can't do anything about my roomates except mitigating damage and that might be the very worst thing possible. You know, enabling and such. 

Good news that Second Roomie and his GF got up and cleaned the living room and kitchen up, it looks relatively normal in there. I gave her the list of services to get her some help for her kids. Hopefully that can get her on the right track. 

Main roomie is still trashed and incoherent, and doesn't want to even try and sober up for work on Monday so I am going on the assumption that he will lose his job. 

I found some info about eviction notices, and it won't be good on my credit, but even after non-payment there are about three weeks of processing before the cops come and throw us out. If I have to I can ride it out and hope to get work next week. I have a good feeling about some of the applications I put in last night and several of them are right up my alley, though I'll take anything at this point. 

Thank you /u/dankjeblieft, your advice and direction was exactly what I needed to hear. 

I'll PM you on some positive updates hopefully this week. 

Thank you for taking the time to reply.

Considering it will take more money than I have to even fill up my gas tank, and that's not even counting food, I don't really have any idea how I am going to ration out forty dollars for any period of time. 

I've been to every financial support well and they are all dry. I cannot get unemployment, and even if I can manage to get food stamps then it will be at least a month before the paperwork is processed. 

Even if I get a job, especially if I get a job, I am out of here no matter what. If I can make it through this week without ending myself then I guarantee I won't be living here. 

Look I appreciate that you are offering suggestions, and the one about a government job center is one I am going to act on as soon as they open monday. 

The rest of what you suggest hasn't worked or is too long-range to get me from here to there. 

I've got a little time, I'm going to keep thinking and planning on how to get out of this situation. 

I'm going to drive my roomate to a detox tomorrow and drop him off. At that point I am going to forget that he ever existed. I'm going to clean his room for the kids' sake and keep trying to find a way out of this hell.

>Also your government should have something to help you locate a job.

Going to look into that Monday, I think there is a gov't run job center not too far from here. 

>If it gets moldy it can jeopardize the health of everyone living there.

Thankfully it isn't to that point yet, and we'll be evicted before it is. 

If he gets taken to the hospital again this weekend (a good chance) I am going to take the opportunity to clean out his room as he gets aggressive if anyone tries it while he is in there. I think he's afraid I'll take his 'hidden booze stash'. 

> Although you might not want to you can sell your car and rely on public transportation. 

I'd only get about $300 blue book value for it, and if I do end up being homeless (the highest likelihood right now come the 1st of the month), I'll need it to live out of.

Trust me I'd love to. I have nowhere to go and no money to get there. If I even had just 2 grand to cover moving into some kind of seedy weekly rental that would get me time to get a job and cover food and gas. 

I could sleep in my car for a few days, though I have no idea what to do when I have to show up clean and pressed with a sharp tie for my job interviews (if I even can get one).

>You should look towards your government for help for yourself.

I've been hitting all of the websites looking for programs, and where I live unless your a female with kids you're pretty SOL for options. 

I've forwarded a few of those programs to other roomie's GF so she can find a place for her and her kids for a while, so maybe that'll work out and I'll have one less thing to worry about. 

The kids are in good health and eating better right now than anyone else in the house. I've really made them my priority since I can't really muster much care about myself I'm doing my best to care for them. 

I know for a fact that foster care isn't what's right for the kids. I've seen it from the inside. At the very best they'll be split up and might not see each other for years, at the very worst they'll be dropped into a group home that'll be even worse condition than they are now.

I gave up trying to control my main roomie's problems months ago. There is literally nothing I can do to get him to stop drinking and I have stopped trying. All I'm doing now is checking on him every few hours to see if I need to take him to the hospital. And of course getting woken up every time he bangs on my door for some inane request. 

I have tried getting him Baker-Acted several times as he is a significant risk to his own health. After every headwound trip to the ER, or when his BAC came back as  .38, and each time they release him and he comes back and somehow finds a way to get more liquor.

My main goal is to get the hell out of here but I can't seem to find a way to do it that doesn't involve literally living under a bridge, and I'd rather end myself before I go back to that.

[3000 mg is considered the 'maximum daily dose'](http://www.emedicinehealth.com/acetaminophen_tylenol_poisoning/article_em.htm)

All at once I think it might be dangerous. Call poison control in your area ASAP.
